27287.description:
Job Type:
Fixed Term Contract
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining the project construction team and reporting to the Registered Mine Surveyor, the primary purpose of this position is providing support in all survey activities, including surface and underground across the organization.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Do Daily face pick-up and mark-up, update of working plans/computer files.
Practical use of the Surpac software including Leica total stations and GPS units, UAV drones etc.
Undertaking a variety of surveys including engineering, construction, and roads.
Undertaking mining and exploration surveys in both open cut and underground.
Collaborating with project staff and seeking advice from Senior Surveyors as required.
Deliver project outcomes in accordance with client specifications and expectations.
Commitment to application of work health and safety principals’ policy.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you have a tertiary qualification in Surveying with MRA Mine Surveyor accreditation, along with experience in either the Mining, Construction, Engineering or Oil and Gas industries. In addition to this you will have some or all the following.
Sound communication skills.
Bachelor’s degree in surveying
MRA Mine Surveyor accreditation preferred.
Minimum of (2) years’ experience in Topography Survey, preferably in the mining industry.
Sound knowledge in regulatory requirements (with respect to Land Use and land Rights/ Acquisition) by the Mining Regulatory Board
Surpac software experience.
Sound knowledge of safe mining practices and mining standards
Strong planning and analytical skills.
A team player with good computer skills.
Able to communicate effectively across all levels.
Minimum of a Class one (1) driver’s license.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP
Apply

27117.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited operates the Kainantu Gold Mine in the Eastern Highlands Province. Since we launched in 2016, we've grown gold production every year, boosting Papua New Guinea's economy. We take pride in supporting your communities, with nearly 94% of our team members being fellow PNG locals.
Looking ahead, we will significantly increase our gold production in the next three years. This expansion means that K92 is a place for building a stable career, contributing to the community, and being a key part of our success.
About the role
The Supervisor – Social Development Program is responsible for coordinating and delivering social programs that strengthen capacity, improve education and health outcomes, and foster inclusive community development. This role ensures that projects are implemented on the ground in line with company commitments under the Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) and community development plans
By supporting the Social Development Programs Standard within the Social Performance Management System (SPMS), the Supervisor contributes directly to the Material Issue: Capacity Building & Social Investment, which underpins sustainable community growth and resilience.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Lead the consistent implementation of social development initiatives across the mine lifecycle, delivering training, awareness, and capacity-building programs for communities (schools, health centres, women, youth, and church groups) to support sustainable outcomes beyond the mine.
Supervise, mentor, and develop Community Development Officers, including work planning, resource allocation, performance feedback, and supporting recruitment and capability building.
Execute program standards and workflows, coordinate field activities (health, literacy, empowerment, youth), track participation and outcomes, produce reports, and ensure compliance with IFC standards and internal commitments.
Collaborate with internal teams, government, NGOs, and community partners to align programs, integrate development initiatives, manage expectations, and deliver against formal social development commitments (MOA).
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential and/or preferred that you:
Have a Diploma or degree in Social Sciences, Education, Community Development, or related field.
3-5 years’ experience in delivering community programs, ideally in PNG or Melanesia.
Proven ability to manage small teams and deliver against workplans.
Strong communication and facilitation skills in Tok Pisin and English; local dialects an advantage.
Experience in conducting baseline studies (community, socio-economic, and spatial context) and social impact monitoring (aligned to projects, operations, and tenements/license/permit areas).
Demonstrates inclusivity, fairness, and respect for diverse community groups.
Builds trust through consistent follow-through and transparent communication.
Acts as a role model of integrity and collaboration in program delivery.
Models K92’s values of respect, accountability, and teamwork
Mining Industry experience preferred. Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.

27562.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The role will provide maintenance planning leadership in support of optimizing the availability andreliability of Mobile Plant and equipment and lead the Mobile Planning Section to ensure that all activities meet the company's business needs, and consistently meet high standards of safety quality and costs.
Essential Duties
Provide coaching, mentoring, and guidance to planning staff in order to foster best practices in planning, scheduling, and utilizing Newmont’s 6 Step work management process.
Always promote and uphold safe working practices and a secure environment for all team members.
Manage the planned maintenance team’s targets and key performance indicators to ensure operational effectiveness.
Ensure that all preventive maintenance programs are executed in accordance with established schedules.
Maintain accurate and relevant historical maintenance records, including associated costs.
Foster positive employee relations by exercising impartial judgment and ensuring fair and equitable treatment of all personnel.
Ensure effective two-way communication is consistently maintained across all groups, sections, and departments.
Embed a culture of best practice and continuous improvement within the Maintenance Planning function.
Conduct annual performance reviews for all direct reports and ensure agreed improvement initiatives are implemented.
Collaborate closely with the Fleet Engineering Superintendent to ensure a consistent and unified approach to all operational tasks.
Provide regular updates and feedback to the Fleet Engineering Superintendent
Training & Experience
Technical experience and knowledge in Heavy Equipment planning and maintenance.
Proficient in the use of the design software Office software (Outlook, Word, Excel, Access).
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Strong planning and organizational skills. In-depth SAP knowledge.
Builds positive working relationships with a diverse range of people across disciplines.
Able to be an effective team member by listening, clarifying tasks, receiving and providing feedback.
Able to be an effective team leader (where applicable) by establishing and maintaining a positive and productive work environment through listening, dealing with different points of view, giving and receiving feedback.
Understands own behaviours and is aware of the impact on others.
Adapts their own behaviour where necessary to get a productive outcome for the wider team.
Working Conditions
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply  before
13th July 2026
– we’d love to hear from you!
Apply

27558.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your impact
As the Supervisor, Laboratory, you will play an important leadership role supporting safe, reliable laboratory operations that contribute to the success of the Lihir operation.
You will guide and support a team of laboratory technicians, building capability, strengthening skills, and ensuring work is completed safely and accurately. Your leadership will help create a respectful and inclusive team culture while driving continuous improvement and delivering results that support the wider site community.
As part of our team, you will
Lead daily laboratory activities to ensure accurate results and smooth workflow
Promote a strong safety-first culture and adherence to site procedures
Support, coach, and develop local talent through mentoring and training
Plan and coordinate team rosters, tasks, and workload
Monitor laboratory equipment and address issues quickly
Communicate clearly on performance, priorities, and results
Manage laboratory resources including consumables and PPE
Work closely with other departments across site
Identify and implement continuous improvement opportunities
Pre-requisites for your success in this role
Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, with proven experience in a mining or processing laboratory environment and demonstrated leadership capability.
Ability to interpret complex laboratory and operational data, identify trends, and apply structured root cause analysis to resolve equipment, process, and quality issues.
Strong hands-on capability to diagnose and resolve technical and quality issues, with the confidence to make effective decisions during critical operational events.
Demonstrated ability to identify inefficiencies and implement practical solutions that enhance safety, quality, and productivity.
Deep understanding of assay laboratory workflows, analytical techniques, with strong capability in KPI reporting.
Strong working knowledge of Quality Management Systems as it relates to ISO 17025
Practical experience operating and maintaining laboratory instrumentation such as AAS, Leco analyzers, fusion and cupellation furnaces and, and UV-Vis spectrometers.
Proficiency in interpreting analytical results and applying Statistical Process Control (SPC) methods to monitor performance and drive  corrective actions.
Proven ability to lead teams, manage performance, coach and develop employees within a team-oriented environment.
Experience using LIMS, SAP, and Microsoft Office.
Your work environment
You will join a supportive and multicultural team environment at Newmont’s Lihir operation, working closely with colleagues across metallurgy, operations, geology and other site functions. You will lead a team of 12 technicians and play an important role in developing local workforce capability.
Working Conditions
This role is offered on a 28/14 (combination day and night), Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. 27557.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your impact
As the Supervisor, Laboratory, you will play an important leadership role supporting safe, reliable laboratory operations that contribute to the success of the Lihir operation.
You will guide and support a team of laboratory technicians, building capability, strengthening skills, and ensuring work is completed safely and accurately. Your leadership will help create a respectful and inclusive team culture while driving continuous improvement and delivering results that support the wider site community.
As part of our team, you will
Lead daily laboratory activities to ensure accurate results and smooth workflow
Promote a strong safety-first culture and adherence to site procedures
Support, coach, and develop local talent through mentoring and training
Plan and coordinate team rosters, tasks, and workload
Monitor laboratory equipment and address issues quickly
Communicate clearly on performance, priorities, and results
Manage laboratory resources including consumables and PPE
Work closely with other departments across site
Identify and implement continuous improvement opportunities
Pre-requisites for your success in this role
Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, with proven experience in a mining or processing laboratory environment and demonstrated leadership capability.
Ability to interpret complex laboratory and operational data, identify trends, and apply structured root cause analysis to resolve equipment, process, and quality issues.
Strong hands-on capability to diagnose and resolve technical and quality issues, with the confidence to make effective decisions during critical operational events.
Demonstrated ability to identify inefficiencies and implement practical solutions that enhance safety, quality, and productivity.
Deep understanding of assay laboratory workflows, analytical techniques, with strong capability in KPI reporting.
Strong working knowledge of Quality Management Systems as it relates to ISO 17025
Practical experience operating and maintaining laboratory instrumentation such as AAS, Leco analyzers, fusion and cupellation furnaces and, and UV-Vis spectrometers.
Proficiency in interpreting analytical results and applying Statistical Process Control (SPC) methods to monitor performance and drive  corrective actions.
Proven ability to lead teams, manage performance, coach and develop employees within a team-oriented environment.
Experience using LIMS, SAP, and Microsoft Office.
Your work environment
You will join a supportive and multicultural team environment at Newmont’s Lihir operation, working closely with colleagues across metallurgy, operations, geology and other site functions. You will lead a team of 12 technicians and play an important role in developing local workforce capability.
Working Conditions
This role is offered on a 28/14 (combination day and night), Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
This position reports to the Senior Geologist Mining and forms part of the Mining team accountable for providing geological and Geotechnical support across the organization.
Observe and adhere to the workplace health & safety policies to ensure safety of employees, contractors, and stakeholders.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Train in all appropriate aspect area of exploration and underground mine geology services.
Undergo training to do all mine sampling activities – not limited to faces, stopes, broken ore, self-mined ore, PAF/NAF, stockpiles on regular basis.
Training on drill core logging, core sampling, density tests – to ensure   correct QA/QC protocols are adhered to.
Train on production data tracking management
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you must have a bachelor’s degree in Geology as minimum. In addition to this, you will have some or all the following.
1+ years relevant mining or exploration work experience.
Able to perform duties under minimum supervision.
Must be a self-starter and very resourceful and of sober habit.
Good health and physical ability a pre-requisite, as is the ability to live in a remote environment with limited facilities.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.

Join High Arctic and play a key role in shaping the future of our growing operations in Papua New Guinea.
For more than 17 years, High Arctic has delivered tailored energy and equipment solutions to Papua New Guinea's oil and gas industry, building a reputation for safety, reliability, innovation, and operational excellence. As our business continues to grow and diversify, we are investing in our people, assets, and maintenance capability to support the next phase of our expansion.

Maintenance Superintendent
to join our Port Moresby team. Reporting to the
Asset Manager
, this is a pivotal leadership role responsible for overseeing maintenance activities across High Arctic's fleet and equipment portfolio, ensuring assets are maintained safely, reliably, and efficiently to support operational performance and future growth.
This is an exciting opportunity to join a business experiencing significant growth in equipment hire activity and maintenance demand. Maintenance workloads are projected to triple across our two support bases. As Maintenance Superintendent, you will be at the forefront of this expansion, providing the leadership, structure, and technical direction required to build a high-performing maintenance function while ensuring our equipment remains safe, compliant, reliable, and ready to support our clients' operations.
Key Responsibilities
Lead, mentor, and develop maintenance teams to achieve safe and efficient outcomes.

A recognised trade qualification or engineering qualification in a mechanical or related discipline.
7–10 years' experience in maintenance operations with leadership experience at Supervisor or Superintendent level.
Strong knowledge of CMMS-driven maintenance environments, asset reliability, and maintenance best practices.
Proven experience leading maintenance teams in safety-critical industries.
Excellent leadership, communication, and stakeholder engagement skills.

Experience within oil & gas, mining, construction, or heavy equipment industries.

Reporting to the Mobile Maintenance Superintendent the Tyre Fitter is responsible for the inspection, fitting, repair, and management of tyres across Tolu Minerals' light vehicle and heavy mobile equipment fleet, ensuring tyres are maintained safely and equipment downtime due to tyre-related issues is minimized.

Heavy Equipment Fitter (HEF) - Underground
Job Title
Heavy Equipment Fitter (HEF) - Underground
Location
Tolukuma Mine Site, Papua New Guinea (Underground Mine)
Department
Mobile Maintenance (M&E)
Roster
19 days on / 9 days off
Reports To
Superintendent - Mobile Maintenance
Company Overview
Tolu Minerals Limited has successfully completed its exploration phase and is transitioning into underground mining operations in Papua New Guinea, with full-scale production targeted for 2027. This role is part of the build-up of operational capability across the Mobile Maintenance Department as the company moves from development into full operational status.
Job Purpose
Reporting to the Mobile Maintenance Superintendent the Underground Heavy Equipment Fitter is responsible for the maintenance and repair of underground mobile mining equipment (jumbos, LHDs, underground trucks, charge-up rigs, and associated plant) operating within Tolu Minerals' underground mine, ensuring equipment is maintained safely and reliably to support production and development activities.
Key Responsibilities
Perform scheduled and breakdown maintenance on underground mobile equipment including LHDs, jumbos, underground haul trucks, and ancillary underground plant.
Diagnose and repair mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, and basic electrical faults on underground mobile equipment in line with OEM specifications.
Carry out maintenance and repairs safely within underground working conditions, including confined spaces, restricted access areas, and ground control zones.
Conduct pre-start checks and condition assessments on underground equipment, reporting defects through the appropriate reporting system.
Complete accurate job cards, work orders, and maintenance records for all underground maintenance activities.
Respond to underground equipment breakdowns promptly, coordinating with the Mobile Maintenance Supervisor and Underground Operations on access and ventilation requirements.
Liaise closely with Underground Operations (Drilling, Exploration) to coordinate equipment access and minimize disruption to production schedules.
Comply strictly with underground ground control, ventilation, and emergency response procedures at all times.
Maintain a safe, organized underground workshop/service bay area and ensure correct handling and storage of fuels, oils, and hazardous substances underground.
Participate in underground safety inductions, toolbox talks, and emergency response drills.
Qualifications
Trade certificate in Heavy Equipment Mechanics / Diesel Fitting or equivalent recognized trade qualification.
Underground mining induction/ticket required, or willingness and ability to obtain prior to commencement.
Current PNG driver's license.
Gas testing and underground self-rescuer training (or willingness to be trained) required.
Experience
Minimum 3 years' post-trade experience maintaining heavy mobile equipment, with prior underground mining experience strongly preferred.
Experience working with underground LHDs, jumbos, and trucks highly regarded.
Demonstrated experience working safely within underground mine environments, including awareness of ground conditions and ventilation requirements.
Skills & Competencies
Strong mechanical, hydraulic, and diagnostic fault-finding skills specific to underground mobile equipment.
Sound understanding of underground mine safety, ground control awareness, and emergency response procedures.
Ability to work effectively and calmly in confined, low-light, and physically demanding underground conditions.
Good communication and radio/communication protocol skills for coordinating work underground.
Strong safety mindset and ability to follow strict permit-to-work and isolation procedures.
Working Conditions
Underground and surface mining environment with exposure to heat, humidity, noise, dust, and confined spaces.
Operates on a fixed roster of 19 days on / 9 days off.
Required to work shift patterns including day and night shift as rostered.
Must comply with all Tolu Minerals HSE policies, PNG Mining Safety regulations, and site-specific permit-to-work systems.
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) is mandatory at all times in designated areas.
Acknowledgement
This job description outlines the general nature and key responsibilities of the role and is not exhaustive. Duties may be amended from time to time in line with operational requirements as Tolu Minerals progresses toward full production.
How to Apply
If you have the skills, experience, and motivation to contribute to the continued success of Tolu Minerals, we would love to hear from you.
Please submit your resume and cover letter outlining the position you are applying for to:
[email protected]
Applications Close:
10th July 2026
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. If you do not receive a response within two (2) weeks of the closing date, please consider your application unsuccessful.
Apply

POSITION TITLE: DRIVER - LAE
CONTEXT
Médecins Sans Frontières (Doctors Without Borders) is a private, non-profit international humanitarian organization, founded in 1971 and working in 70 countries around the world. MSF provides medical assistance to populations in crisis, regardless of race, religion, belief or political affiliation. In PNG, MSF has been working since 2007 in Lae, Tari, Bougainville, Gulf Province and NCD Province. MSF is now working to support the Department of Health to improve access to care for patients in Lae, Jiwaka and Highlands.
MAIN PURPOSE OF THE POSITION:
Performing the tasks of transporting authorized goods and passengers in an
MSF
vehicle, ensuring its technical and safety conditions and respecting the country's traffic rules and
MSF
security rules, in order to provide a safe, smooth and efficient service
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Checking daily, the technical conditions of the assigned vehicle (state of the tires, oil, fuel, brakes, radio equipment, spare parts, vehicle body etc.), performing weekly check according to the MSF Logbook, refilling it when necessary, and keeping it clean to ensure it can be driven in perfect conditions.
Carrying out a proper handover of the vehicle from one driver to another during shift/ driver change.
Ensuring the security of passengers in the vehicle, driving carefully, observing speed limits and traffic rules in the country as well as MSF security rules, in order to avoid car accidents.
Ensuring all passengers have all necessary paperwork in order before travelling and ensuring non-MSF staff sign discharge of liability before using the vehicle.
Ensuring that all vehicle documents and the driver's driving license are valid, up to date and stored the vehicle.
Informing the line manager of any incident involving the transportation of passengers and/or goods.
Knowing how to use all types of radios, codes, call numbers and radio alphabets by heart and communicating with base according to MSF communications policy to inform the driver's position and any potential implications.
Knowing and respecting the security rules related to vehicle movements, specifically those related to customs, checkpoints and roadblocks. Ensuring all passengers know and respect the security rules.
Good knowledge of roads in Morobe and its environs.
Ensure comprehensive handover is conducted between drivers during shift/ driver change.
Renewal of your driver’s licence before its expiration.
Monitoring the fuel gauge levels to ensure refuelling is done in a timely manner; and monitoring vehicle maintenance to know when it is close to the service km/period and inform the Logisitcs Supervisor/ Manager.
Proper recording of fuel dispensed into vehicle in the vehicle’s fuel log book.
Respect of defined MSF speed limits.
Ensure vehicle doors are locked when passengers enter the vehicle and seat belts worn by all passengers before driving.
Proper recording of movements with clear name, destination, time and signature of passengers in the vehicle logbook.
Daily inventory of the vehicle’s tools during handover. Every Equipment and Tool handed over in the vehicle should be carefully used. Equipment and tools in the vehicle are not to be taken out for personal use or used in another vehicle without approval from the Logisitcs Supervisor/ Manager.
Responsible for cleaning of MSF vehicles and basic maintenance (state of the tires, oil, fuel, brakes, radio equipment, spare parts including tire, vehicle body etc.).
Adhereance to operational instructions and responsibilities given by the Logisitcs Supervisor/ Manager.
Adherence to MSF standard operating procedures, guidelines, security rules and confidentiality.
Perform duties observing MSF policies and in compliance with relevant SOPs of the department and immediately reporting to supervisor whenever compliance is or cannot be met.
SKILLS AND REQUIREMENTS
Education
Essential secondary school certificate and valid driving license.
Experience
2 years minimum of previous driving experience.
Good knowledge of country roads.
Previous experience with MSF or other NGOs.
Languages
English and Tok Pisin
Knowledge
Competencies
Essential knowledge of basic mechanics
Good knowledge of mission area roads
Results and Quality Orientation, Teamwork and Cooperation, Behavioral Flexibility, Commitment to MSF Principles, Stress Management
Competencies
Results and Quality Orientation, Teamwork and Cooperation, Behavioral Flexibility, Commitment to MSF Principles, Stress Management
WORKING CONDITIONS
Fixed term Contract
Based in Morobe
Candidates must be flexible with working hours and location

MSF is committed to safeguarding, protection and fulfilling duty of care to patients, all people and communities we serve, and our staff. All staffs are required to share this commitment through signing and complying with our Behavioural Commitments and all relevant safeguarding policies.
Furthermore, receiving MSF job offers will be subject to satisfactory professional reference checks and clean criminal clearance.

27380.description:
POSITION TITLE: EXECUTIVE PRINCIPAL, BALIMO COLLEGE
AREA:
Education
LOCATION:
Balimo College, New Town, Balimo, Delta Fly District, Western Province PNG
TYPE / DURATION:
Full time, 1 year contract, with contract extension possible
REPORTING TO:
Chair, Balimo College Governing Council
About Balimo College:
Balimo College’s vision is to advance Western Province by providing high-quality teaching, research and community engagement. The institute will foster pathways of teachers and health workers who are committed to improving access to vital services in Western Province. Balimo College will be a safe and supportive place for graduates and other professionals across the Western Province catchment region to return for life-long learning and ongoing professional development. The College will develop a community of education and health professionals committed to innovation, excellence and community advancement; by being the training College of choice for Papua New Guineans
Balimo College is an initiative of SDP implemented in partnership with KTF. SDP has a mandate to deliver development programs which provide lasting benefits to the people of Western Province. Our efforts are focused on Health, Education, Infrastructure and Agribusiness. We aim to supplement and complement the efforts of the Fly River Provincial Government (FRPG), in other words, help fill the gaps in the existing systems.
Balimo College is recognised as a Higher Education Institute by the National Higher Technical Education Board of the Department of Higher Education, Research, Science and Technology (DHERST). This recognition has been granted in accordance with the provisions of the Higher Education (General Provisions) Act 2014, as amended in 2020, under Section 14(1)(i) and 55(4)(a).
About the Role:
The Executive Principal is responsible for leading the strategic direction, operations, and administration of both the School of Teaching and the School of Nursing. Reporting to the Chair of the Governing Council, the GM will ensure that the College’s mission, vision, and goals are effectively upheld across all departments, ensuring high standards of education and community service. The GM will lead the executive team, including the Principals of both schools, and oversee all administrative, financial, and human resources functions.
The GM will have an in-depth knowledge of the ethos and purpose of the Balimo College and the principles by which it operates. The GM will have a firm understanding of the Western Province education and health contexts and the objectives of Balimo College to create pathways for rural communities into teaching and community health work.
Responsibilities:
Leadership & Strategy
Lead the strategic development and implementation of Balimo College’s vision, mission, and values.
Supervise and support the Principals of the School of Teaching and School of Nursing, ensuring alignment with institutional goals.
Foster collaboration between the schools to create a cohesive, innovative, and community-focused institution.
Establish and nurture a positive and inclusive college culture, promoting care, academic excellence, and integrity.
Drive initiatives to improve academic offerings, operational efficiency, and community engagement.
Operational Management
Ensure effective daily operations of Balimo College, including the coordination of academic programs, facilities, and student services.
Lead the College executive team to optimize the performance of both schools and streamline administrative processes.
Oversee the development and implementation of college policies, procedures, and systems in consultation with the two Principals, and in alignment with governing regulations and standards.
Coordinate the preparation of the academic calendar in collaboration with leadership teams.
Ensure compliance with PNG Department of Higher Education, Research, Science & Technology (DHERST) and other relevant authorities.
Human Resources and Capacity Building
Manage the recruitment, induction, and evaluation of staff in both schools in collaboration with the Principals and Governing Council.
Develop a performance management system and provide ongoing professional development opportunities for staff.
Foster leadership and career development among faculty and support staff.
Chair Staffing Committee meetings, overseeing decisions related to staffing structures, promotions, and performance.

Work with the Finance Manager and Finance, Audit & Risk Management Committee to develop and manage the College’s budget, ensuring financial sustainability.
Monitor and review financial performance, ensuring that spending aligns with the College’s strategic goals.
Act as a responsible signatory for financial decisions within the limits established by the Governing Council.
Academic Oversight
Ensure that the College’s educational programs meet high standards of quality and relevance to the community’s needs.
Oversee curriculum development and academic planning, in consultation with the two Principals, ensuring alignment with national and international standards.
Chair the Academic Board and receive reports from the Principals of the School of Teaching and School of Nursing in line with the Academic Board charter.
Foster partnerships with external stakeholders, including universities, government departments, and donors, to enhance the College’s programs and resources.
Community Engagement & Stakeholder Relations
Act as the primary spokesperson for Balimo College, building relationships with community leaders, government partners, and external partners.
Ensure active engagement with the local community to strengthen the College’s role as a hub for lifelong learning and professional development.
Promote and sustain a safe and inclusive environment for students, staff, and the broader community.
Risk Management & Compliance
Ensure adherence to all risk management, safety, and compliance requirements, particularly in workplace health and safety (WHS), child protection, Code of Conduct and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment.
Work with the Finance and Risk Management Committee to develop and implement a risk management framework.
Ensure that Balimo College operates in accordance with its safeguarding Policies, safeguarding the well-being of all students and staff.
Required Skills and Attributes:
Knowledge of:
A strong understanding of tertiary education and the specific challenges and opportunities in rural Papua New Guinea.
Experience in leadership roles within education, health or public sector institutions, preferably in PNG or similar contexts.
Proven financial management skills and experience managing budgets for educational institutions.
Familiarity with government policies and standards for tertiary education (DHERST, NDOE, PNG Nursing Council).

Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with diverse stakeholders.
High integrity, resilience, and the ability to lead by example. Applicants must have the right to work in PNG.

27535.description:
Officer – Media and Communications
About Us
New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea (PNG). As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. Our commitment to safety, innovation, and responsible mining ensures that we not only contribute to the economy but also support the development and prosperity of the regions we operate in. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.
New Porgera Limited now has a vacancy for a qualified and experienced individual to join our
Media and Communications Department
as
Officer – Media and Communications.
About the role
Reporting to the Superintendent – Media and Communications, the successful applicant will supports the development and delivery of internal and external communication strategies. The role ensures timely, accurate and culturally appropriate communication across the business, while assisting in media management, content creation, and stakeholder engagement to promote transparency, operational awareness and corporate reputation.
In this role, you will;
Produce compelling visual and written content that reinforces NPL’s reputation as a responsible operator.
Ensure all public-facing materials directly support the company’s right to operate by highlighting ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) milestones and community success stories.
Ensure all communications align with corporate brand standards and messaging guidelines
Deliver consistent internal newsletters, print, and audio-visual content that ensures NPL’s workforce understands operational goals, safety standards, and company news.
Provide fit-for-purpose materials (posters, community flyers, and brochures) that allow the company to maintain a respectful, transparent presence with landowners and local authorities.
Ensure local stakeholders have a clear, non-technical understanding of the mine’s activities, reducing the risk of community grievances through proactive information sharing.
Maintain and update company website and social media platforms.
Monitor digital engagement metrics and provide basic analytics and reporting.
Ensure timely and appropriate responses or escalation of public inquiries.
Assist in implementing crisis communication plans during operational incidents.
Prepare draft communication materials for emergency situations.
Ensure accuracy and timeliness of information released to stakeholders.
Ensure communications comply with company policies, PNG regulatory requirements, and confidentiality standards.
Maintain proper records of communications and approvals.
Maintain media contact lists, communication calendars, and document archives.
Support logistics for communication campaigns, events, and site visits
Maintain a high level of health and safety awareness and comply with NPL Occupational Health & Safety Policy and all health rules and procedures
About You
To succeed in this role, the ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications and experience;
Bachelor’s Degree in Communications, Journalism or related discipline
3–5 years’ experience in communications, media, public relations, or stakeholder engagement, preferably within the resources, mining, or industrial sector.
Experience in community engagement and stakeholder relations is required. Work experience with communities in PNG is an advantage.
Excellent writing, editing, and content development skills, with strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office, content management systems, social media platforms, audio-visual editing tools, and digital analytics platforms.
Strong knowledge of media relations, brand management, SEO, accessibility standards, and digital communications best practices
Advanced skills in graphic layout, design, and visual content production.
Demonstrated cultural awareness, ability to work effectively in PNG’s diverse environment, and capacity to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced operational setting with minimal supervision.
Mobilization Requirement
This is a PNG National position, a site-based role on a FIFO arrangement with a rotation of 21 days on and 14 days off. Candidates must successfully pass a pre-employment medical, including drug and alcohol screening (to be arranged only for successful candidates after the interview stage), and provide an up-to-date Police Clearance Certificate (acquired within the last 6 months). Candidates must be PNG Nationals and available to start immediately. Females are encouraged to apply.
Join Our Team as a
Officer – Media and Communications.
Embark on a rewarding career with New Porgera Limited as an Officer – Media and Communications
.
This role offers a unique opportunity to work with a dynamic team to contribute to NPL’s success. Enjoy a balanced work schedule, competitive compensation, and a chance to develop your career and technical expertise in a supportive and professional environment.
Note:
This advert will be open until
10
th
July 2026
. If you do not hear from NPL within next two (2) weeks following the closing date, please consider your application unsuccessful for this opportunity.
External Application URL:
Officer – Media and Communications
Apply

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Ensure secure operation by fulfilling end user requirements for timely availability of materials from the warehouse and to carry out the receipt, storage, issue, and dispatch of materials in a safe and efficient manner whilst adhering to site policies and procedures.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Receive, store, issue and dispatch of operational spares and consumables to ensure continuous production at all times.
Unpack, sort and checking of goods received for quality, quantity and specification.
Complete stock taking as directed by the Supply Superintendent and Supply Manager
Support the implementation of supply process improvements.
Investigate invoice discrepancies relating to receipting issues.
About You
To be considered for this position, candidates should be able to demonstrate experience in a warehousing environment where they have used computerized stock and inventory control systems and they have gained a good understanding of warehousing concepts and techniques. In addition to this, candidates should also (ideally) be able to demonstrate some or all of the following.
Knowledge and experience with use of Pronto and Microsoft office
Competence in operation of materials handling equipment. (Eg: Forklift truck).
Good interpersonal and communication skills.
A good understanding of relationship between warehouse operations and successful business performance.
Skills in risk awareness and hazard identification.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.

We’re Hiring | Management Accountant | Lae, Papua New Guinea
Are you an early-career accountant looking to build real commercial skills — not just process transactions, but genuinely understand how a business works?
Spectra Industrial Limited is one of Papua New Guinea’s leading importers and distributors of industrial equipment. We sell, hire and service power generation equipment, material handling equipment and construction machinery. We also supply genuine spare parts and provide after-sales technical support, end-to-end solutions for our customers, and a genuinely diverse finance environment for our team.
We’re growing — Our finance team is growing with us. And we have a Management Accountant role that puts you at the heart of how this business performs.
The Role
Working closely with the Financial Controller, you will own a meaningful piece of the numbers from day one. You will carry direct responsibility for management accounts, inventory costing, fixed assets and compliance in a business with real commercial complexity.
Key Responsibilities
Prepare monthly management accounts — P&L, balance sheet and variance analysis.
Own inventory costing and margin reporting across equipment categories (generators, forklifts, construction machinery and hire fleet).
Maintain and reconcile inventory records against the general ledger, coordinate and report on periodic stock takes.
Manage the fixed asset register — additions, disposals, depreciation schedules and physical asset verification.
Drive month-end and year-end close processes, including journal entries and account reconciliations.
Handle GST reconciliations and ensure compliance with statutory tax obligations.
Liaise with Sales, Operations and Procurement to support financial reporting and resolve queries.
Contribute to audit preparation and internal control improvements.
Deliver ad hoc financial analysis and reports to senior management.
Qualifications & Experience
Degree in Accounting, Finance or a related field.
1-3 years’ experience in an accounting role, or a strong recent graduate ready to step up.
Working towards CPA or an equivalent professional qualification (encouraged, not mandatory).
Solid Excel skills, experience with Odoo is a genuine advantage.
Sharp attention to detail and a personal commitment to accuracy.
Clear communicator — comfortable working with non-finance teams in Sales and Operations.
Self‑driven and commercially curious; focused on understanding the business rather than merely reconciling it.
Compensation & Career Growth
Competitive salary commensurate with experience.
Direct mentorship from seasoned finance professionals.
Broad commercial exposure — inventory, fixed assets, compliance and management reporting, all in one role.
A diversified, growing industrial business with genuine long-term career opportunity.
A team that backs initiative and rewards performance.

27574.description:
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The Services Technician will operate the assigned sections of the process plant (Grinding circuits, flotations, thickener operations, flotation reagent preparations and mill reline activities) so that all Safety & metallurgical targets are met on a shift-by-shift basis.
Essential Duties
Champion a strong safety culture by ensuring full compliance with all HSE policies and Fitness for Work standards.
Perform tasks only when hazards and risks are clearly understood, working closely with Supervisors to confirm safe controls.
Proactively monitor plant operations and implement strategies to minimise risks and maintain a safe working environment.
Promptly report hazards, unsafe behaviours, and incidents in line with company standards.
Collaborate effectively with diverse teams across departments to support operational success.
Take ownership of your area, consistently delivering on commitments and maintaining high performance standards.
Engage in ongoing development through training, shift handovers, toolbox talks, and team activities.
Maintain high housekeeping standards within the process plant at all times.
Operate plant equipment in line with daily plans and inspections, identifying and escalating defects or risks as required.
Ensure all shift activities—including inspections, operational tasks, and SOP adherence—are completed safely and in full compliance with environmental and company guidelines.
Training & Experience
Prior experience in mineral processing
Tertiary qualification advantageous.
Certificates/Statements of Attainment in relevant metalliferous processing competencies highly regarded.
Minimum level of Grade 10 education desirable.
PNG driving License class 6
Good verbal & written communication skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work autonomously from time to time.
High attention to detail with good time management skills.
Strong active listening & interpersonal skills.
Working Conditions
This is a FIFO role on a 28/14 rotating roster.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!
Apply

27514.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
Step into a role where your financial expertise directly shapes business performance. As a Specialist, Finance based in Brisbane, you will partner closely with site leadership based in Papua New Guinea to deliver critical insights, drive cost control, and support multimillion-dollar capital investment decisions.
You will play a key role in coordinating budgeting and forecasting and SOX compliance, delivering accurate month-end reporting, and identifying opportunities to improve financial processes and reporting standards. Your work will enable better decision-making across operations, ensuring financial discipline and long-term value creation.
As part of our team, you will
Partner with operational leaders to prepare annual budgets and rolling forecasts, aligning inputs across multiple departments
Deliver accurate month-end financial reporting and analyse cost and capital expenditure variances
Provide actionable financial insights and recommendations to drive site performance and business outcomes
Support and manage capital expenditure pipelines, contributing to effective financial planning
Identify and implement process improvements to strengthen financial reporting and analysis practices
Build dashboards, analytical models, and forecasting tools using SAP, Power BI and advanced Excel
Collaborate with department managers, superintendents, and stakeholders to embed strong cost control practices
Present financial performance insights to senior stakeholders to influence decision-making
Prerequisites for your success in this role
To thrive in this position, you will bring a combination of technical capability, strong stakeholder engagement, and the ability to operate independently:
Qualifications & Experience
Degree in Accounting or Finance, with CA/CPA (or working towards)
Demonstrated experience in financial planning & analysis, ideally within mining or heavy industry environments
Exposure to capital expenditure analysis and cost management
Technical Expertise
Strong experience with SAP (S/4HANA preferred) and financial systems
Advanced Excel skills, with experience in building financial models
Power BI capability, including training users and troubleshooting
Capabilities & Attributes
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to draw insights from complex data
Confident communicator, able to engage stakeholders in both on-site and virtual environments
Self-driven with the ability to work independently and manage competing priorities
Collaborative mindset with the ability to influence and build relationships across teams
Your work environment
You will join a collaborative, outcomes-driven finance team supporting a dynamic mining operation. Working closely with departmental leaders, senior finance professionals, and site stakeholders, you will contribute to a high-performing and supportive culture.
This role offers the opportunity to work on a significant capital portfolio, providing exposure to complex financial challenges while partnering with experienced leaders. You will also benefit from flexible working arrangements and the ability to collaborate effectively across geographically dispersed teams.
Working conditions
12-month fixed-term opportunity, with potential for extension or permanency.
You must have the legal right to work in Australia to be considered.
Our Brisbane-based team enjoys flexible Monday to Friday work arrangements, balancing time between the office and working from home. Our modern Fortitude Valley office is conveniently located near public transport and local cafés. Occasional travel to site operations and other interstate Newmont hubs may be required to support the broader team.
Why Join Newmont
Work on impactful, high-value capital projects
Partner with strong, supportive leadership
Gain exposure to a global mining environment
Enjoy flexibility while building your career in a critical finance function
Submit your application through our website quoting reference number 43515 before the advertised closing date: 8 July 2026
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!
Apply

More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
As K92 continues expanding our underground gold mine near Kainantu, safety remains our number one priority, as such, we seek to add an additional Senior Safety Officer to the team who will be responsible for ensuring that all safety regulations and procedures are followed at our Kainantu Gold Mine. This role is a crucial role in preventing accidents and incidents, protecting the health and safety of employees, contractors and maintaining compliance with Papua New Guinea’s safety laws and regulations.
Key Accountabilities
Ensuring the continuous improvement of, safety inspections, safety training and compliance.
Maintain a safe work environment for all K92 employees, visitors and contractors through audits, inspections, and training.
Maintain the efficiency and cost-effective management of safety in the workplace and project site.
Ensure all incidents are fully investigated and recorded within the site safety data base in a timely and accurate manner.
Development of safety training programs and initiatives.
Develop scheduled, weekly, monthly safety audits and checks project wide
Collate and submit weekly and monthly reports to Project Director and Operational GM.
Attend site wide weekly and monthly safety meetings.
Ensuring that the camp and project sites safety regulations are observed by all K92 employees including contractors,
Provide safety induction to new intakes, casuals, contractors, and visitors to site.
To ensure the safety rules and other policies of the camp and mine site are observed and report any suspicious activities
About You
To be considered for this role, you must have a Degree or Diploma in Health & Safety/Environmental Health from a recognized institution or equivalent., in addition you must have some or all of the following
At least 10 years’ experience in occupational health and safety in mining environment would be an advantage A Diploma or certificate in Health Extension or General Nursing is an advantage.
Current PNG Driver’s license.
Training and Assessment experience and qualifications.
Possess good training skills
Completion of accredited fire training.
Current first aid certificate.
Well-versed experience in project safety management.
Excellent oral and written communication skills.
Proficient in computer and e-mail correspondences.
Ability to meet communicated schedules and deadlines.
Strong planning, interpersonal and organizational skills
Exposure to Emergency Response teams, processes.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP
Apply

27530.description:
Advisor - Business Development
About Us
New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. Our commitment to safety, innovation, and responsible mining ensures that we not only contribute to the economy but also support the development and prosperity of the regions we operate in. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.
The New Porgera Limited now has a vacancy for a qualified and experienced individual to join our Community Relations Department as
Advisor – Business Development.
About the role
The Advisor – Business Development, is responsible for designing, developing and implementing good governance mechanism, commercial compliance obligations, financial empowerment, and generally acceptable business development practices. The Advisor will be the primary contact between NPL and local SMEs interfacing to ensure they’re sustainably positioned to operate a thriving business beyond the mine life. Reporting to the Senior Advisor, the role ensures meaningful partnerships with business communities, agencies of government and key stakeholders to deliver measurable business development impact. The role crosscuts into supporting National Content agenda of NPL towards fulfilling its reporting obligations.
In this role, you will
Support, mentor, and build capacity of landowner businesses, local SMEs, NGOs, and entrepreneurs in the following critical areas
Business registration and compliance (IPA, IRC, TIN, COC, Insurances).
Develop and establish relevant policies to improvement governance, business management, finance, human resource management, assets and inventory controls, safety management, etc.
Reporting: Monthly or annual management accounts, bank reconciliations, annual reports, and corporate income tax returns, etc.
Preparations for AGMs, Board, and Shareholder meetings.
System set-up such as payrolls, bookkeeping, cash management systems, recruitment processes, etc.
Conduct supplier business baseline capacity assessments to identify gaps in operational capacity, business skills, governance, and financial management.
Facilitate and deliver training sessions, workshops, and advisory support on topics such as governance, charters, policies, business planning, board reports, financial management, procurement, and tax compliance.
Ensure that supported businesses are fully registered with the Investment Promotion Authority (IPA) and meet ongoing Internal Revenue Commission (IRC) obligations.
Guide local companies on the preparation and submission of required corporate governance documents, annual returns, and tax compliance records.
Assist businesses in developing and submitting proposals for mine procurement opportunities.
Provide advice and introduction for accessing loans support and investment capital.
Monitor and document business development progress, prepare reports, and escalate issues early.
Qualifications & Experience
Degree in business administration, Accounting, SME Development, or related field.
3–5 years’ experience working directly with small businesses or economic development programs.
Demonstrated ability to advise on governance, compliance, and finance for micro and small enterprises.
Solid understanding of PNG’s legal and tax framework for SMEs.
Excellent interpersonal and facilitation skills across diverse cultural settings.
Ability to work independently in the field and maintain accurate documentation.
Proficiency in English and Tok Pisin
Key Competencies
Strategic thinking
Cultural sensitivity
Generally accepted business principal skills
Financial literacy
Communication and presentation skills
Risk assessment and mitigation
Mobilization Requirement
This is a PNG National position, a site-based role on a FIFO arrangement with a rotation of 21 days on and 14 days off. Candidates must successfully pass a pre-employment medical, including drug and alcohol screening (to be arranged only for successful candidates after the interview stage), and provide an up-to-date Police Clearance Certificate (acquired within the last 6 months). Candidates must be PNG Nationals and available to start immediately. Females are encouraged to apply.
Join Our Team as an
Advisor – Business Development
Embark on a rewarding career with New Porgera Limited as a Advisor – Business Development This role offers a unique opportunity to work with a dynamic team to contribute to NPL’s success. Enjoy a balanced work schedule, competitive compensation, and a chance to develop your career and technical expertise in a supportive and professional environment.
