27504.description:
“Join our team to support creating more inclusive workplaces in Papua New Guinea!
Commencement: August 2026
Locally engaged Consultant – 6 Months (Flexible work arrangement available)
Based in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea
Open to all candidates
*Abt is committed to advancing women’s leadership in PNG’s economic development and are building an environment where women can lead progress and shape economic outcomes. Abt promotes an inclusive, respectful and safe working environment for women and encourages PNG women and men to apply.
This position includes health insurance and supportive workplace for parents and carers, including relevant leave and other benefits including shuttle services to and from work.
About the Program
The
Australia–Papua New Guinea Economic Partnership (APEP)
is a flagship partnership supporting Papua New Guinea’s economic development priorities. Delivered by the Government of Australia in close collaboration with the Government of Papua New Guinea, APEP focuses on strengthening economic systems, institutions, and opportunities that support sustainable and inclusive growth through to 2028.
Working alongside government, research institutions, and development partners, APEP delivers coordinated and high‑impact outcomes across four key engagement areas:
Safeguarding Macroeconomic Stability
Supporting More Efficient and Inclusive Markets
Fostering Inclusive Growth and Expanded Livelihoods
Catalysing Economic Research and Dialogue
Gender equality, disability social inclusion (GEDSI), women’s economic empowerment, and climate are central to APEP and integrated across all engagement areas and activities.
About the Opportunity
The Department of Agriculture and Livestock (DAL) supported by the Australia – Papua New Guinea Economic Partnership, seeks a highly qualified Legal Expert to provide comprehensive legal counsel and drafting support for the finalization of the National Seed Policy. The expert will join the Seed Policy Technical Working Group (TWG) to ensure that all proposed policy mechanisms, regulatory frameworks, and legislative clauses are robust, enforceable, and fully aligned with Papua New Guinea’s constitutional framework and administrative law traditions.
The Legal Expert will act as the primary interface between the TWG’s technical agricultural objectives and the statutory requirements of the State of Papua New Guinea. The core objective is to ensure that the new policy does not merely exist on paper but is practically and legally ready for institutional implementation.
This position will play an important role to ensure the effective and efficient implementation of this project and will coordinate implementation of the project activities and deliverables as per the project plan and results framework.
Key responsibilities
Regulatory Gap Analysis:
Conduct a comprehensive audit of existing agricultural legislation, land use laws, biosecurity and trade regulations to identify potential conflicts or redundancies with the proposed Seed Policy.
Consultation & Validation:
Attend all TWG meetings and sit in on regional stakeholder consultations and validation workshops to provide real-time legal input on proposed mechanisms and address stakeholder concerns regarding legal enforceability.
Legislative Drafting:
Act as a key member of the Drafting Committee to finalize the statutory text of the National Seed Policy, ensuring clarity and legal precision. Translate technical policy recommendations into formal statutory text, ensuring legal precision and adherence to standard drafting practices for PNG legislation.
Institutional Alignment:
Assess the mandates of relevant agencies (e.g., DAL, PNGBA, NARI, NISIT, etc,.) to ensure the proposed seed system governance does not create jurisdictional friction.
State Solicitor Liaison:
Manage direct technical reviews and consultations with the Office of the State Solicitor to ensure the drafted policy meets all requirements for government adoption.
Conflict Resolution:
Provide legal memoranda regarding any conflicting mandates or constitutional impediments identified during the policy development phase.
Policy Finalization & Submission:
Provide legal support throughout the finalization process and assist in the formal submission of the policy to the Secretary of the Department of Agriculture and Livestock (DAL), the Minister for Agriculture, and the National Executive Council (NEC).
Other activities of a similar nature requested by the Agricultural Growth & Livelihoods Team Leader
About You
For applications to be considered,
a response to the Key Selection Criteria below must be provided
.
Education:
Bachelor of Law (LLB) from a recognized university; admission to the PNG Bar is required.
Experience:
Minimum 7–10 years of professional experience in legislative drafting, commercial law, or administrative law, preferably within the PNG public sector or for international development agencies.
Technical Knowledge:
Demonstrated understanding of PNG’s constitutional framework and the legislative process (including the role of the Legislative Counsel), and the requirements for NEC submissions.
Agricultural Insight:
While technical agricultural knowledge is provided by the TWG, the candidate should demonstrate an ability to quickly grasp the complexities of seed systems, biosecurity, and agricultural trade.
Collaborative Capability:
Proven ability to work effectively alongside international technical experts and cross-functional teams in high-stakes project environments.
Soft Skills:
Strong negotiation skills, proficiency in report writing, and the ability to bridge technical jargon/agricultural requirements with clear legal language.
“
We value capability and potential, and welcome applicants who believe they can succeed in this role”
How to Apply
Please ensure to address the Key Selection Criteria (About You) in your cover letter, and submit your application online, along with your CV as a single document.
Applications must be submitted personally by individuals only. Applications submitted by a company or organisation will not be accepted.
The successful applicant will be engaged through an employment agreement determined by Abt.
We welcome and thank all applications; however, only shortlisted applicants will be contacted
.
Closing Date: Sunday, 5 July 2026 (Midday, local time)
#LI-AUSBRIT
Abt Global is an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to upholding high standards of Child
Protection, Anti-bribery and Fraud Protection.
We encourage applications from experienced and capable women, and people with disabilities

27534.description:
Looking for a Change?
Join CARE International in PNG and be part of an organisation that serves the needs of Papua New Guineans living in remote PNG.
EXTERNAL RECRUITMENT
Project Coordinator – BECOMES Project
CARE International in PNG is looking into recruiting a qualified and a suitable candidate for its
Bougainville Cocoa Families Support (BECOMES)
Project Coordinator role based in Arawa, ARoB. CARE is an international development and humanitarian aid organisation fighting global poverty, with a special focus on working with women and girls to bring lasting change to their communities. As a non-religious and non-political organisation, CARE works with communities to help overcome poverty by supporting development efforts and providing emergency assistance. We believe supporting women and girls is one of the most effective ways to create sustainable outcomes in poor communities.
CARE International in Papua New Guinea has a focus on Gender Equality, Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Climate Change Adaptation (CCA), Agriculture and Health.
BECOMES Phase four (4) aligns with the Bougainville Agricultural Commodities Regulatory Act (2020) and Cocoa Regulations (2022) by strengthening farmer-group compliance, quality assurance, record-keeping, business capacity, and links to value-added markets. The project will support
40 target groups
through tailored packages:
31 Bougainville Partnership (BP)-linked groups
— comprising
12 Commodity Support Facility (CSF) grant-recipient groups
and
19 Innovation Stream groups
— plus
9 additional groups
to be jointly confirmed by
CARE, BP, Department of Primary Industries and Marian Resources  (DPIMR) and Department of Commerce, Trade, Industry and Economic Development (DCTIED)
.
The Project Coordinator (PC) will oversee the Project’s Phase IV activities in support of farming groups and families. This will largely be coordinating training and other activities with a stronger focus on farmer-group governance, inclusion, market readiness and sustainable transition. Working with the Program Manager, it will also include supporting the overall planning, development, coordination and implementation of project activities. We are seeking an experienced and driven Procurement Manager with construction experience to lead complex procurement activities for our Company. In this pivotal role, you will be the key point of contact for all Procurement related activities, ensuring all materials purchased meet technical specifications, financial targets, and regulatory requirements. Your leadership will be critical in guiding the Procurement team from the initial planning stages through to final handover of projects.
Role Overview
As Procurement Manager, you will be responsible for leading the Company’s procurement department, ensuring the timely, cost-effective, and compliant acquisition of goods and services. Your role involves developing strong sourcing strategies, managing supplier relationships, negotiating contracts, and ensuring adherence to procurement policies and regulatory requirements.
Reporting to
: Group HR & Administration Manager
Key Responsibilities & Duties
Lead end-to-end procurement processes including RFP/RFQ management.
Develop strong sourcing strategies to optimize cost, quality, and supply reliability.
Conduct market analysis to identify trends, risks, and opportunities in supplier markets.
Identify, evaluate, and qualify suppliers based on capability, financial stability, compliance, and performance
Manage supplier relationships to drive performance improvement, risk mitigation, and continuous improvement.
Monitor supplier performance against agreed KPIs and service level agreements.
Negotiate commercial terms and conditions to secure favourable pricing, delivery, and legal terms.
Ensure all contracts are executed in accordance with company policy and legal standards.
Monitor procurement spend and identify cost reduction initiatives without compromising quality or compliance.
Ensure all procurement activities comply with internal policies, ethical standards, and applicable laws and regulations.
Maintain accurate records and documentation for audit and reporting purposes.
Implement and monitor procurement controls to prevent fraud, waste, and abuse.
Partner with internal stakeholders to understand requirements and align procurement plans with business needs.
Provide guidance and training on procurement policies and processes.
Provide Weekly and Monthly Reports

Qualifications & Requirements
Bachelor’s degree in business administration, commerce, or a related discipline.

Proficient in MS Office Suite, specifically Excel, Word and Outlook. Experience with and ERP system would be an advantage.
Demonstrated understanding of procurement principles, purchasing processes, and vendor management.
Essential Skills & Competencies
Exceptional leadership and team management abilities, with a focus on mentoring and developing talent.
Superior communication, negotiation, and vendor relationship management skills.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a keen attention to detail.
Ability to multi-task and strong delegation skills.
What We Offer
Competitive remuneration package
Opportunity to contribute to a growing nationally owned company
Professional and respectful working environment
Opportunity to play a key role in strengthening organizational systems

Looking for a Change?
Join CARE International in PNG and be part of an organisation that serves the needs of Papua New Guineans living in remote PNG.
EXTERNAL RECRUITMENT
Woman’s Economic Empowerment & livelihood Officer – THRIVE Project
CARE International in PNG is seeking a qualified and experienced Project Officer to support the effective coordination and implementation of the Transforming Health, Resilience, and Inclusion through Village Empowerment Program. CARE is implementing the THRIVE Project in Upper Bena Rural LLG, Eastern Highlands Province, to improve community health, well-being and resilience. The project focuses on safe water, hygiene and sanitation, maternal well-being and women’s economic resilience, responding to community – identified priorities such as unsafe water access, water-related illness, limited health access and livelihood security.
The Project Officer (WEE and Livelihood) will support community mobilisation, activity facilitation, data collection, participant follow – up and day-to-day field coordination to ensure activities are delivered safely, respectfully and in line with CARE’s standards for safeguarding, GEDSI, accountability and do-no-harm programming.
The Project Officer will support field implementation of the THRIVE project by working directly with communities, local stakeholders and project participants to deliver inclusive health promotion, hygiene and sanitation awareness, maternal well-being support, VSLA activities, financial literacy and women’s livelihood strengthening.
This role is based in Goroka and will require travel to field sites in Upper Bena LLG, Unggai Bena District in Eastern Highlands Province.
EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS:
Relevant qualification in public health, community development, gender and development, social sciences, project management, rural development or related field.
At least 2 to 3 years of experience supporting community-based development, , livelihoods, gender or women’s economic empowerment projects
Experience facilitating community awareness sessions, training, mobilisation, household engagement or group-based activities in rural communities
Experience working with community leaders, women’s groups, youth groups, churches, health workers, volunteers, local government stakeholders or community-based organisations
Basic understanding of gender equality, disability and social inclusion, safeguarding, protection, accountability and community - led development principles
Experience supporting VSLAs, financial literacy, health promotion, hygiene and sanitation or livelihood activities will be an advantage
CORE COMPETENCIES
Good facilitation, communication, community mobilisation and interpersonal skills
Ability to work respectfully and effectively with diverse community members, including women, young people, older people and people with disabilities
Good organisational skills and ability to support field activity planning, logistics and documentation.
Ability to work as part of a team and follow agreed workplans, procedures and reporting requirements
Ability to travel and work in rural and remote communities, including under challenging field conditions
Commitment to CARE’s values, safeguarding standards, gender equality, inclusion and accountability to communities

Help ensure safe, reliable and efficient plant performance
Build your career with a company committed to safety and reliability
About the Company
Our client operates within the energy and power generation sector, delivering reliable power solutions to support business operations and community development. With a strong focus on safety, operational excellence, and continuous improvement, the organisation is committed to maintaining high-performance assets and providing a safe working environment for its employees
.
About the Role
We are seeking a skilled and safety-focused Mechanical Technician to join a power generation team. Reporting to the senior Operations & Maintenance Coordinator, this position is responsible for maintaining and repairing the mechanical systems that generate electricity, including turbines, generators, pumps, and auxiliary equipment. You will play a key role in supporting reliable plant operations, maintaining equipment performance, and contributing to a safe and efficient working environment.
Key Responsibilities
Diagnose and repair mechanical failures, including rotating and reciprocating equipment.
Implement preventative maintenance plans to minimise downtime and ensure equipment longevity.
Repair or replace defective equipment identified through inspections or reported failures.
Perform installation, maintenance, inspection, repair, and testing of cooling, heating, mechanical, electric driven pumps, fans, and compressors.
Maintain accurate maintenance records, work orders, and equipment history reports
Read and interpret technical drawings, specifications, manuals, and maintenance procedures
Ensure all maintenance activities are completed in accordance with safety standards and operational procedures
Work closely with other technicians, operator, engineers, to achieve operational goals
Utilizes precision instruments to ensure proper installation belts, chains, coupling, bearings, and other drive components. Replaces and adjusts packing and seals
Works with equipment which includes diesel engines, emergency generator, reverse osmosis and EDI water treatment systems, air compressors, motors, pumps, etc.
Contribute to a safe and clean work environment through strong housekeeping and safety practices
Requirements of the Role
Technical qualification in Mechanical Engineering, Mechanical Trade, or a related discipline
Over 3 years relevant Maintenance experience in similar roles in the Power Generation industry.
Experience working in power plant environments with Solar Turbines, generator turbines, and control systems.
Strong fault-finding, troubleshooting, and diagnostic skills
Must be familiar with Power Plant CMMS, MS Office applications, and general computer use as well
Sound understanding of workplace health, safety, and environmental requirements
Ability to work effectively both independently and within a multidisciplinary team
Good written and communication skills

An updated CV in Microsoft Word format, outlining employment history, educational qualifications, and listing three referees (referees will only be contacted if shortlisted)

Procurement Officer
Nature of Work
Save the Children is the world’s largest independent child rights development organisation, making a difference to children’s lives in more than 120 countries. From emergency relief to long-term development, Save the Children secures a child’s right to health, education and protection. Save the Children PNG is committed to being a platform for transformative and lasting change for children, their families and their communities. Save the Children prides itself in being a child safe organisation.
Role Purpose
This position is based in our Buka Office and reports directly to the Field Office Manager, with a dotted reporting line to the Supply Chain Manager.  The Procurement Officer is responsible for ensuring that all Save the Children’s procurement policies, processes, and procedures are followed when procuring goods and services for the country offices programmes and operations, and that all processes follow an underlying principle of value for money.
Key Areas of Accountability
Implement procurement activities and services as needed and requested for Save the Children programmes and operations.
Ensure adherence to Save the Children policies, principles and procedures at all times when conducting procurement activities.
Support, demonstrate, and uphold the principle of value for money in all procurement activities.
Initiate and maintain constructive relationships with existing suppliers, while assisting with the exploration of new supplier relationships.
Assist in identifying and implementing both standard and innovative approaches to improving the efficiency of procurement activities, such as the increased use of framework agreements, etc.

27483.description:
Lawyer – Commercial Services
About Us
New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. Our commitment to safety, innovation, and responsible mining ensures that we not only contribute to the economy but also support the development and prosperity of the regions we operate in. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.
The New Porgera Limited now has a vacancy for a qualified and experienced individual to join our
Commercial and Contract Services Department
as
Lawyer – Commercial Services.
About the role
Reporting to the Head of Legal, the successful applicant will join a dynamic team and will be responsible for assisting with providing advice to management and the mine’s various departments across site.  The successful applicant must have a strong character and must be committed to confidentiality and ensuring statutory and internal company policy compliance.  It is essential that the successful applicant is motivated and committed to achieving team objectives.
In this role, you will
Conduct and support litigation under the supervision of the Head of Legal, particularly at the District Court level.
Provide legal assistance and advice to site-based functions on routine matters, including HR issues, Mining Safety Act compliance, and otherlegal queries.
Review and support preparation of low-risk, low-value contracts (e.g., donations, agreements with local landowners).
Attend and support site teams during inspections by regulatory authorities or audits.
Assist the Supply Chain team with vendor compliance and “know your customer” (KYC) processes.
Prepare legal memoranda and conduct research as directed by the Head of Legal.
Engage with the community and other internal / external stakeholders where directed by the Head of Legal;
Assist with the development, implementation and maintenance of safe work procedures and promote high safety and health awareness;
Promote and comply with NPL’s PNG Occupational Health and Safety policies; and
Ensure the appropriate facilitation of procedures and workforce competence to achieve legal compliance, incident prevention and the achievement of tasks in an environmentally sustainable manner
Maintain a high level of health and safety awareness and comply with NPL Occupational Health & Safety Policy and all health rules and procedures
About You
To succeed in this role, the ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications and experience
You will demonstrate a ‘One Team’ approach, providing effective leadership and development for your local team to reinforce NPL’s culture and values, always promoting a safe work environment.  The position requires a high energy individual, hands-on management style and desire to continuously improve you and your team’s knowledge and systems and methods of work.
Qualifications & Experience:
Bachelor’s Degree in Law (LLB)
Admitted to practice law in Papua New Guinea and holds a current practicing or has the ability to obtain a PNG practising certificate;
3-5 years of experience in commercial, corporate or employment law (preferably with experience in the resource sector);
Commercial litigation experience at the District and National Courts of PNG;
Strong knowledge of labour, employment, commercial, and contract law;
Experience in dispute resolution, managing litigation files and exposure to mediation would be an advantage;
Holds a valid driver’s licence;
The ability to work honestly and transparently with minimal supervision and be of sober habits;
An excellent command of English and Tok Pisin, both written and spoken and must be willing to work with and engage with the community; and
Advanced skills in Microsoft Office, Outlook, Excel & Power Point.
Mobilization Requirement
This is a PNG National position, a site-based role on a FIFO arrangement with a rotation of 21 days on and 14 days off. Candidates must successfully pass a pre-employment medical, including drug and alcohol screening (to be arranged only for successful candidates after the interview stage), and provide an up-to-date Police Clearance Certificate (acquired within the last 6 months). Candidates must be PNG Nationals and available to start immediately. Females are encouraged to apply.
Join Our Team as a
Lawyer – Commercial Services.
Embark on a rewarding career with New Porgera Limited as a Lawyer – Commercial Services
.
This role offers a unique opportunity to work with a dynamic team to contribute to NPL’s success. Enjoy a balanced work schedule, competitive compensation, and a chance to develop your career and technical expertise in a supportive and professional environment.

. If you do not hear from NPL within next two (2) weeks following the closing date, please consider your application unsuccessful for this opportunity.

27512.description:
With more than 40 years of experience working in PNG, World Vision International Papua New Guinea (WVIPNG) focuses on helping the most vulnerable children and adults experience fullness of life.  Inspired by our Christian faith, WVPNG has an exciting opportunity for someone who may be looking for a change and wants to become part of a dynamic team helping vulnerable people and communities.
World Vision International Papua New Guinea (WVIPNG) has exciting opportunity for those of you who want a change and want to become part of a dynamic team. We are currently looking for suitable, qualified, experienced, and highly motivated professional to fill the role of
Monitoring & Evaluations Officer
to be based in
Madang Province, Papua New Guinea.
PURPOSE OF THE POSITION
The position holder will be responsible for the qualitative and quantitative measurement and documentation of the achievements of the project through a regular data collection and management process in line with established World Vision PNG M&E framework and Indicator Tracking Table and LEAP Framework.
MAJOR ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
To understand project design and participate in planning and project activity implementation:
Read and understand project design document such as project DIP, project budget and the proposal narrative (PDD).
Actively participate in monthly project
implementation planning and resourcing in collaboration with project supervisor.
Develop tools for the baseline assessment, mid-term and end lines.
Collection & finalizing of baseline data in consultation with project partners to ensure the plan & agreement is in place.
Develop tools for monitoring the knowledge, attitudes and perception of stakeholders on the quality of services being provided by the provincial staff and communities.
Train project field staffs and project coordinator on what data to collect every month and update progression results based on project DIP and ITT.
Support other M&E staffs to design monitoring tools to monitor progress of projects and design evaluation tools to conduct baseline surveys and end of project evaluation as required by WV PNG Program Quality Department.
Quality Assurance and Database Management:
Maintain systematic database system that will allow generation of specific project progress monitoring and evaluation information whenever needed such as;
Develop and maintain names and personal details of registered cocoa and vanilla farmers
Develop and maintain cocoa budwood gardens and cocoa nurseries records.
Develop and maintain training records of cocoa and vanilla farmers who attended integrated cocoa and vanilla pest & diseases management trainings, cocoa value chain management trainings, budwood & nursery management trainings, design and construction of solar dryer trainings etc…group and records of performances of each savings of savings groups and restart new savings cycles.
Network good performing savings groups to micro-banks for the savings group members to access banking services.
Review and Evaluation:
Conduct supervisory and monitoring visits to project sites according to the monitoring and evaluation
Participate in Technical Working Group (TWG) meetings to provide technical reports and updates to operation.
Coordinate with Horizon Coordinator to design TORs for project evaluation and monitoring visits.
Participate in project design workshops.
Staff capacity building on M&E process and tools:
Develop specific data collection tools and train project field staff how to use the data collection templates to collect specific data for each project activity undertaken on a monthly basis.
Develop project ITT and train project field staff on what specific data to be collected that can be fed into the project ITT on a monthly basis.
Train project how to write most significant change stories to show impacts of the project.
Building of personal and organizational capacity in M&E which will reflect in quality programming
Facilitate WV’s Development Program Approach with technical support, capacity building and coaching in collaboration with the M&E Coordinator
Facilitate DME training sessions for staff upon request and on and as need be basis.
When Sector Coordinators aren’t available,
Represent WV at key stakeholder meetings
Project Closeouts, Evaluations and Learning:
Implement project evaluations efficiently
Develop evaluative TORs for end-of-phase evaluations with directions from the M&E Coordinator & Innovation and Impact Team Leader and are in line with LEAP and PTL guidance
Work together with external consultant evaluators involved in evaluations and training.
Participate in providing feedback on project evaluation and baseline reports
Facilitate Learning events in collaboration with the M&E Coordinator for direct & partner implemented projects before the closure of the project in order to document learning and best practice for future programs.
Organize all M&E data, reports, and records for WASH sector and for other projects where needed and archived in a central location for future reference.
EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION/SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE
Possess a Bachelor’s Degree in Statistics, International Development, or Social Sciences or equivalent.
At least 3 years’ experience in design and implementation of M&E in development projects.
Experience in design and implementation of M&E systems; including qualitative and quantitative approaches to assessment and monitoring is required.
Experience in SPSS tools/ EPI Info/ any other similar software.
Experience in data processing or analysis (Excel, etc.) is required.
Detail oriented and able to verify data.
Experience in designing tools and strategies for managing information system, data collection, analysis and production of reports.
Excellent knowledge of monitoring and application of methodology
Desirable to have experience incorporating gender consideration strategies into monitoring efforts of international development projects;
Experience in analyzing data
Strong facilitation skills
Excellent communication skills both written and oral in English
Strong experience with monitoring and evaluating livelihood projects and or grant funded projects
Experience in use of M&E tools and development and use of online tools for monitoring and evaluation activities.
Knowledge in information management and analysis systems including SPSS and MS Access, an advantage
Proficient in MS Excel, Word and PowerPoint.
Highly analytical with a keen eye for details and trends
A competitive salary, benefits, and career development opportunity will be offered commensurate with relevant experience, knowledge, and qualifications.

one PDF file
before;
Wednesday 1 July 2026

Detailed CV

World Vision is committed to safeguarding all children and adults living where World Vision operates. 27491.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The Mechanical Technician will execute safe and effective mechanical maintenance activities to support the reliability, integrity, and availability of fixed plant equipment across operational areas. Perform planned, breakdown, and corrective maintenance tasks in accordance with maintenance strategies, procedures, and work management processes to minimise downtime and support continuous plant operations. Contribute to defect identification, equipment improvement initiatives, and quality maintenance execution while maintaining compliance with safety, environmental, and operational standards.
Essential Duties
Conduct routine mechanical inspections across operational equipment and record findings to support proactive and planned maintenance activities.
Execute and assist with breakdown, corrective, and preventative maintenance tasks to restore equipment reliability and operational performance.
Perform maintenance activities in accordance with site safety standards, isolation procedures, statutory requirements, and company maintenance practices.
Support Rotable Refurbishments, Fixed Crane Maintenance, and Fixed Compressor Maintenance activities to ensure equipment availability and reliability targets are achieved.
Maintain accurate maintenance history and equipment records through effective documentation of repairs, inspections, adjustments, and component replacements within maintenance management systems.
Monitor equipment condition and performance trends, identifying defects, risks, and early signs of failure, escalating findings and recommendations to Supervisors for intervention planning.
Assist with calibration, testing, and commissioning activities to ensure equipment operates within required performance and operational standards.
Support spare parts and inventory management through tracking component usage and identifying critical spares requirements for maintenance activities.
Promote a strong safety culture by actively participating in safety interactions, toolbox meetings, hazard identification, and continuous improvement initiatives aligned to FRM objectives.
Training & Experience
Significant demonstrated experience in fixed plant maintenance within heavy industry or mining environments, including Fixed Cranes and Compressor maintenance activities.
Proven experience maintaining and repairing fixed plant equipment including valves, gearbox drives, conveyor systems, pulleys, sprockets, pumps, feeder tracks, interstage screens, vibrating screens, fixed cranes, and compressors.
Relevant Mechanical Trade Certificate or Engineering Certificate essential, with PNG Driver’s Licence – Class 6 required.
Sound understanding of safe work procedures, lifting equipment operations, and site HSE requirements.
Competent in the use of maintenance tools, equipment, and maintenance management systems including SAP and Microsoft Office Suite.
Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving capability with the ability to proactively resolve maintenance issues.
Effective verbal and written English communication skills with the ability to work across diverse cultural environments.
Strong interpersonal and active listening skills with the ability to work collaboratively within team environments.
Demonstrated ability to manage time effectively, adapt to operational changes, and support continuous improvement and waste reduction initiatives.
Works in accordance with PNG Mine Safety Act, Newmont Standards, Safety Policies and Procedures, Newmont Environment policies and all departmental operating procedures.
Skilled in the use of SAP sofware.
Uses interpersonal negotiation skills and influencing skills to maintain the agreed breakdown work against weekly schedules.
Demonstrated knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite, specifically Word and Excel.
Working Conditions
This is a FIFO role on a 28/14 rotating roster.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!
Apply

27440.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
In this critical leadership role, you will drive the success of mobile asset management and shutdown execution by ensuring the efficient coordination and delivery of kitting and staging activities. You will lead a high-performing warehouse team, enabling the safe, timely and cost-effective preparation of materials that support operational continuity across site.
Your ability to lead people, optimise processes and collaborate across functions will directly influence safety outcomes, operational efficiency and overall business performance.
As part of our team, you will
You will play a key role in leading warehouse operations and ensuring the seamless execution of kitting and staging activities:
Oversee and coordinate kitting and staging activities to support mobile asset management and shutdown execution.
Monitor progress, plan workflows and ensure alignment with operational schedules.
Supervise contractor activities and support execution teams during mobile asset management and shutdown delivery.
As a people leader, you will:
Lead, coach and develop a team, building capability and driving performance outcomes.
Foster a positive, safe and productive team environment grounded in accountability.
Set clear expectations and promote continuous improvement across the team.
You will also contribute to operational excellence by:
Ensuring compliance with safety standards and proactively identifying risks.
Reviewing performance outcomes and implementing improvements to optimise efficiency.
Collaborating with maintenance, mobile asset management and shutdown teams and key stakeholders across site.
Supporting delivery across safety, cost, people and productivity priorities.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
To succeed in this role, you will bring strong leadership capability combined with practical experience in warehousing and logistics:
Demonstrated experience in logistics, warehousing, supply chain or a related field, with progression into leadership roles.
Strong stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to collaborate across functions and influence outcomes.
Proven ability to lead and develop teams in a fast-paced operational environment.
You will also demonstrate:
Knowledge of SAP systems and strong proficiency in Excel and reporting tools.
Experience in warehouse operations, including kitting, staging and shutdown preparation activities.
Understanding of mobile fleet servicing, parts management and shutdown processes.
Strong planning, coordination and organisational capability.
In addition, you will bring:
Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills, with the ability to work autonomously.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including conflict resolution capability.
A proactive and solutions-focused mindset, with a strong commitment to safety.
High levels of integrity, accountability and professionalism.
Your work environment
Based at Lihir Operations, you will work within a dynamic and fast-paced warehouse and logistics environment. You will collaborate closely with supervisors, superintendents, maintenance teams and project teams, as well as external contractors and suppliers.
This is a hands-on leadership role within a supportive team environment, where safety, performance and collaboration are key to success.
Working Conditions
This role is offered on a 21:21 (day shift) Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, you will be part of a global organisation committed to safety, operational excellence and continuous improvement.
This role offers:
The opportunity to lead a critical function supporting key operational deliverables.
Exposure to complex logistics and warehouse operations.
A collaborative and inclusive team environment.
